text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Frederick Chiluba assures miners that the privatisation of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) will not lead to job losses and is designed to resuscitate the economy.
- A non-governmental organisation involved in reforming sex workers say the capital, Lusaka, has at least 4,000 prostitutes who service, on average, seven men a night.
- The Zambia Congress of Trade Unions decries job insecurity and harsh conditions Zambian faced by Zambian workers.
- Boart Longyear, a subsidiary of Botswana's Boart Drilling (Pty), is awarded a $15 million contract at the recently-sold Konkola North and Kansanshi mines.
- Interpol impounds 25 motor vehicles suspected to have been stolen from neighbouring countries.
- The immigration department deports 24 Zaireans for illegal entry.

- The Zambia Congress of Trade Unions says the growing number of illegal vendors in urban centres is a sign of economic weakness while president Frederick Chiluba says they are a vehicle for development.
